title: See whether a dashboard stays focused

blocks.content: The dashboard's title, Grafana Dashboard, doesn't say what question it answers. You have to read the panel titles, Memory / CPU, server requests, and logins, to learn that it's about a server's resources and traffic.
The title says exactly what the graph represents, and the values carry a unit, bytes, so the viewer doesn't have to think about it.

Both the logins and server requests panels show the server's traffic, and both titles tell you what the graph represents at a glance. Their values on the y-axis are plain numbers with nothing after them. Requests and logins are counts, things you tally, so there's no unit to show.
View the first **Google hits** bar gauge.

Here's a vertical bar gauge with five bars labeled A-series to E-series. Nothing says what each bar measures. Its unit is percent on a fixed 0 to 100 range, but hits are a count, not a share of anything. So the label is misleading.
Now, notice the second **Google hits** bar gauge.

Here's the same five unnamed bars, this time with no unit, still on a fixed 0 to 100 range. The colors change at 40, 60, 70, and 80. But with no unit, the viewer can't tell what the color changes mean.
Next, look at the **Google hits** gauge.
This gauge suggests a value approaching a limit. The limit is 300 with no unit, and the single series is labeled A-series. Nothing on the panel says what 300 hits would mean.
Focus on the third **Google hits** bar gauge.
Here's a horizontal bar gauge with six bars named for servers, Backend-ops-01 to Frontend-web-02. The names help, but there is still no unit.

Four panels, one title, no descriptions. A viewer must figure out what each one represents and how they differ. That is cognitive load the dashboard adds instead of reducing.

A focused version would keep **Memory / CPU**, **Memory**, **server requests**, and **logins**, and drop the **Google hits** repeats.
